Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a concise measurement matrix and an invitation plan for read-only dashboard access. High-level answers first, then the matrix attached.

1) Availability definition
- Availability = successful customer-visible requests / total customer-visible requests in the period. We exclude internal health checks and control-plane-only traffic. We compute region-level availability and a global SLA derived from weighted regional traffic.

2) Latency measurement
- We report P50/P95/P99 on end-to-end inference tail latencies (request accepted to final token), measured at the edge that serves customer traffic. Standard SLA commitment includes P95 < 1200ms for standard models; custom commitments are listed in contract.

3) Monitoring & hosting
- Metrics pipeline: service -> Prometheus -> long-term ingest in our TSDB -> Grafana (customer-facing readonly instances are federated via secure links).
- We can create a time-bound read-only Grafana invite scoped to your account and a throttled query quota. See attached grafana_invite_instructions.txt.

4) Alerting
- We push alerts to Opsgenie and PagerDuty, and can offer webhook delivery to your incident system. Default severity mappings and escalation policies are documented in the attached playbook.

5) Exceptions
- Temporary SLO exception: we support a documented exception for up to 30 days, with owner (customer success) and compensating controls (increased logging, optional managed runbook). Extensions beyond 30 days require Legal and Reliability approval; credits are handled per our SLA credit policy.

I attached a compact SLO measurement matrix (slo_measurement_matrix.xlsx) with formulas and examples you can paste straight into your procurement package. If helpful, I can also share the read-only Grafana invite once you confirm the user email(s).

Next steps
- Confirm one or two viewer accounts for the Grafana invite.
- Let me know if you need sample alert rules in Opsgenie format.

Thanks — Kim
